### CANDIDATE DETAIL
#### 1. hereditary spastic paraplegia 8  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.689)
**Link type:** shared causal gene (HGNC:28984)

**Proposed mechanism:** WASH complex subunit 5 (HGNC:28984) —DISRUPTS→ WASH complex (GO:0097059); WASH complex (GO:0097059) —DISRUPTS→ Actin dynamics regulation (GO:0030777); Actin dynamics regulation (GO:0030777) —DISRUPTS→ Vesicular trafficking (GO:0006898); Vesicular trafficking (GO:0006898) —LEADS_TO→ Neuronal development and function (HP:0007156); Vesicular trafficking (GO:0006898) —LEADS_TO→ Craniofacial abnormalities (HP:0000256). Loss-of-function mutations in WASHC5 disrupt the WASH complex, leading to dysregulated actin dynamics. This, in turn, impairs vesicular trafficking, contributing to both the neuronal defects seen in hereditary spastic paraplegia 8 and the craniofacial abnormalities characteristic of Ritscher-Schinzel syndrome 1.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of individuals with pathogenic variants in WASHC5 exhibiting only one of the two disease phenotypes, or exhibiting phenotypes not explainable by impaired vesicular trafficking or actin dynamics. _(variant: Exome sequencing data from gnomAD showing a common variant (AF > 0.01) in WASHC5 that is strongly associated with either Ritscher-Schinzel syndrome 1 or hereditary spastic paraplegia 8, but not both.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of WASHC5 in vesicular trafficking and actin dynamics provides a potential therapeutic target for both Ritscher-Schinzel syndrome 1 and hereditary spastic paraplegia 8 by aiming to restore normal cellular transport mechanisms.
